link_coverage.exhausted_reason: This link is exhausted by construction, not by a thin search. The parties that own the Russian refining capacity whose attrition sets demand for every other link on this chain are Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft, Surgutneftegas and Tatneft. The London Stock Exchange suspended the admission to trading of every one of their depositary and ordinary lines, and the UK, US and EU have since imposed asset freezes, OFAC blocking sanctions and a full transaction ban on the largest of them. There is therefore no public legal issuer on this link that resolves to a validated public listing reachable by a non-sanctioned investor, and the chain's own ticker list for this link is deliberately empty for the same reason.

audit.independence_limitation: The semantic review was conducted in a dedicated fresh context limited to CLAUDE.md, method.md section 6A, the atlas-cartographer contract, this mapping, its chain, the tools/check_map.py and universe-gate.py gate contract, and the source URLs currently named by placement and EXHAUSTED evidence, without the author transcript, map log, profiles, screens, or ledger rationale. Method section 6A states a COMPLETE map has no OPEN links and has passed this semantic audit; with 12 OPEN links this map fails that gate by construction regardless of citation quality. Because this audit issued FAIL solely on the OPEN-link/COMPLETE gate and not on any evidence defect, its clean sampled_checks (41 of 41 true, zero identity/role/source-date conflicts) remain informative for the next author pass: nothing sampled here needs re-verification, only new coverage needs to be added.

notes.text: Identity is legal-entity based and every counted listing is proved by a verbatim span copied out of a securities filing that was actually fetched and text-extracted in this run, not from a search snippet. The exchange field carries the exchange name exactly as the filing prints it, which is why it reads 'New York Stock Exchange' rather than the NYSE shorthand used in earlier maps: the excerpt has to state the exchange the listing claims, and inventing a shorthand the source never used would break that. One disclosure a later audit needs: sec.gov and data.sec.gov both return HTTP 403 to this venue, so most of these filings were opened through a third-party document mirror rather than the regulator's own host. The document at each URL is the registrant's own Form 10-K or Form 20-F and every excerpt was text-extracted from the fetched file, but the host is a mirror and the audit should re-open these URLs on that understanding.

What this census cannot see, stated plainly. This chain is 61 percent non-US by ticker, and the official identity sources for those listings are the ones that defeat automated reading: sec.gov, data.sec.gov, nyse.com, hkex.com.hk, londonstockexchange.com company pages, nseindia.com, tmx.com and the JPX client portal all returned either HTTP 403 or a JavaScript shell with no instrument record in it. Euronext returned a page without the symbol field. The only official listing source that survived at scale was the securities filing itself, which biases this run's completed coverage toward SEC registrants. Eleven of the thirteen links are therefore left OPEN rather than closed: OPEN here means the census is genuinely incomplete, not that the universe is small. The links that need non-US identity work first are hydroprocessing-catalysts, the money corner, which holds one issuer where the real universe also contains BASF, Clariant, Johnson Matthey, Sinopec and JGC; and shipyard-newbuild-capacity and refinery-capacity-response, which have no placements at all because every credible name on them is Korean, Chinese, Japanese or Indian.

russian-refining-attrition is the one link that is genuinely closed, and it closes at zero. That is not a gap in the search: the chain's own note says the ticker list is deliberately empty because Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft and Surgutneftegas are sanctioned, and the search record proves it from two independent directions, an official exchange suspension notice and a dated sanctions analysis. The link that sets demand for the whole chain has no instrument, which is exactly the ARCH-003-inverted shape the chain already names.

Second pass, aimed at the only two link_coverage rows that had neither a placement nor an EXHAUSTED search, which is the state a fresh context audit can never sample. refinery-capacity-response now carries four issuers and shipyard-newbuild-capacity two. Both rows stay OPEN, because OPEN here is the honest reading: the real universe on each link is larger than what this run could prove, so EXHAUSTED would be a lie about the world rather than a statement about the census. Four channels answered this venue and are worth recording for the next run: the BSE corporate filings archive at bseindia.com, which serves SEBI LODR letters whose headers print the legal issuer, the exchange and the NSE symbol together; HKEXnews at hkexnews.hk, whose announcement covers print the exchange disclaimer, the legal name and the stock code on one page; Japanese earnings reports hosted on the issuer's own investor site, whose header block prints listed company name, listed exchange and stock code; and issuer hosted SEBI filings such as BPCL's own results letter.

What this pass still cannot see, named issuer by issuer so the gap is falsifiable. shipyard-newbuild-capacity is dominated by Korea and by China's A share yards, and neither could be admitted. For Korea, HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (009540), Samsung Heavy Industries (010140), Hanwha Ocean (042660) and HD Hyundai Mipo (010620) all exist and all belong on this link; the sources tried and refused were englishdart.fss.or.kr (the filing viewer renders a shell with no stock code or market), global.krx.co.kr (404), data.krx.co.kr (a JavaScript shell), englishkind.krx.co.kr (no such host) and the issuers' own English IR dataroom pages, which load their document lists by script. kind.krx.co.kr does render, but only in Korean, and admitting a Korean language legal name would split issuer identity across the corpus. For China, China CSSC Holdings (600150) publishes no English filing at all; CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering is admitted in its place because it is the same group's H share listed yard vehicle and files in English. Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd. was researched and refused on one exact point: the SGX announcement page and the FY2025 annual report each carry two of the three required identity fields, the announcement page printing the legal issuer and the counter code BS6 without ever naming the exchange, and the annual report naming Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited without ever printing BS6. Cochin Shipyard Limited was researched, and its identity is provable from bseindia, but it was left off because its merchant order book is 1,700 TEU feeders and 26 metre tugs, which are not the berths that gate clean product tanker fleet growth. Sumitomo Heavy Industries was researched and rejected on its own words: its financial report records orders decreasing partly due to withdrawal from the new shipbuilding business. On refinery-capacity-response, Reliance Industries appears in the chain's example tickers for this link and was deliberately NOT placed: its 2025-26 integrated annual report shows no new conversion capacity of its own, so placing it here would have been padding. Saudi Aramco, Thai Oil, Petrobras and Chennai Petroleum were each attempted and each failed on one reachable identity document (Aramco's report sections time out, the SET pages return a rendered summary rather than a verbatim record, sec.gov returns 403 to this venue and Petrobras's mirrored 20-F exceeds the fetch size limit).
